chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Al-Subah ibn Sayyaba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever says, when he prays the Maghrib prayer, three times: 'All praise is for Allah, who does what He wills, and He alone does not do what others will' (or: 'and He does not do what He wills, unlike others'), will be given abundant goodness.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite after the Maghrib prayer for receiving abundant goodness?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the spiritual efficacy of reciting a specific dhikr emphasizing Allah's absolute agency ('Yaf'alu ma yasha'u') three times after Maghrib. The phrase 'wa la yaf'alu ma yasha'u ghayruh' underscores divine omnipotence by negating independent will in creation, a concept deeply resonant in Shia theological reflections on God's decree. The promise of 'abundant goodness' reflects the tradition's emphasis on consistent, post-prayer devotions as a means to secure both spiritual and worldly blessings.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Al Sabbah Bin Sayaba, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who says, when he prays the Maghrib Salāt, three times, ‘The Praise is for Allahazwj who Does whatever Heazwj so Desires to, and does not Do what others desire’, would be Given a lot of goodness’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma’Il have narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from al-Sabbah ibn Sayabah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Whoever, after Maghrib prayer, says three times, ‘All praise belongs to Allah, Who does as He wills and does not do what others will,’ will receive a great deal of good.”
